title: The role of mitochondrial energy metabolism in drug resistance and prognosis of lung adenocarcinoma: a multi-omics and machine learning strategy for predictive and personalized therapy.
summary: Using single-cell RNA-sequencing and TCGA-LUAD data, the authors built a five-gene LASSO-Cox prognostic classifier, MDrisk, from mitochondrial-metabolism and drug-resistance features. Scores were associated with immune and tumor-genomic features and computationally inferred drug sensitivity; ALDOA silencing was followed by reduced lung-adenocarcinoma cell proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro. This does not show patient treatment benefit.
ai_technology: The MDrisk five-gene prognostic classifier was selected using LASSO-Cox and combinations of machine-learning algorithms applied to mitochondrial-metabolism and drug-resistance features.
organization: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Tangdu Hospital, The Fourth Military Medical University; School of Medicine, Northwest University; Department of Ophthalmology, Tangdu Hospital, The Fourth Military Medical University

evidence.tested: The primary article reports MDrisk development from single-cell RNA-sequencing and TCGA-LUAD data, assessment in training, internal-test and external GEO cohorts, associations with immune and tumor-genomic features, and computationally inferred drug sensitivity. In vitro ALDOA silencing experiments assessed lung-adenocarcinoma cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Drug sensitivity was computationally inferred; the study did not test whether MDrisk-guided therapy improves patient outcomes.
evidence.unknown: Drug sensitivity was computationally inferred, and cell experiments do not establish clinical treatment benefit or patient outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: The MDrisk five-gene prognostic classifier was selected using LASSO-Cox and combinations of machine-learning algorithms applied to mitochondrial-metabolism and drug-resistance features.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
